date_note: Security NEXT, published 20 November, reports Soft99's disclosure but gives no announcement date; the contractor alerted Soft99 on 5 November and the company reported to the Personal Information Protection Commission on 9 November.
title: Soft99: unauthorized file on online shop, personal data of up to 136,968 customers may have leaked
summary: Security NEXT reports that Soft99 disclosed an unauthorized file, described as a backdoor, on its official online shop after a contractor alerted it on 5 November. Personal information of up to 136,968 registered customers who bought by 5 November may have leaked, including names, addresses, birth dates, purchase history and partial card data. The shop was suspended; the cause is under investigation.
plain: Japanese car-care company Soft99 says a hacker's file was found on its online shop and data of up to 136,968 customers may have leaked.
exec: A retailer's web shop was compromised, putting up to 136,968 customers' personal data at risk.
action: Soft99 customers: watch for phishing that uses your name or purchase details, and check card statements for unfamiliar charges.

validation.note: Only Security NEXT read, relaying Soft99's disclosure; Soft99's own notice was not found.
